barRaise.topFinding: Five real fixes are done on disk, and none of them exists anywhere but this one tree. The commit-per-patch rule this project wrote for itself has been broken for at least eight days, which is exactly the state it exists to prevent on a mount where an interrupted write truncates a file. The work itself is good: damage logic moved into the defense system, the publish strips its administrator-only section before reaching the gated worker, the target picker stopped sorting when it did not need to, a licence gate refuses release while the obligation stands, and the sandbox preset gained a version plus an atomic write. Run the release and all five become real.

the watchdog now lives outside the registry it watches: X:\Claude\registry-heartbeat.py runs hourly from the native Windows task claude-registry-heartbeat, registered by X:\Claude\register-registry-heartbeat-task.ps1 at 20 past the hour and verified running with LastTaskResult 0 at 00:55 on 2026-09-05. It checks the task-folder count under C:\Users\Kane\.claude\scheduled-tasks, parses the live registry, requires a firing inside 30 hours, and requires the backup chain to be under 48 hours old and to hold a full roster. Failure raises four channels: a Windows toast, X:\Claude\REGISTRY-HEARTBEAT-ALERT.md, CLAUDE-ROUTINES-STOPPED.txt on the desktop, and a line in X:\OPEN-LOOPS.md that the [loops] hook prints at every session start; --test-alert fired all four and the first healthy run withdrew them, restoring OPEN-LOOPS.md byte for byte. routine-health-watch gained a bullet reading registry-heartbeat-state.json, so a dead heartbeat is itself detected. Commit cd1d32d in X:\Claude.

Closed as unrecoverable, not as fixed. This was reopened earlier on 2026-09-22 because a foreign project's queue row had closed it on a colliding finding identifier, which is not evidence. The reconstruction then failed: no bar-raise report in this repository carries an entry under this identifier, the ledger holds no prior evidence, and the title was overwritten by the reopening note, so nothing anywhere records what the finding said. There is no defect to verify and none to fix. Reopening it was right and leaving it open is not: an item nobody can read is not work, it is a row. The project's next review re-raises it with its own evidence if the underlying defect is still there, and the identifier collision that caused this is itself closed, since reconcile-status-queue.py now keys a close on the project as well as the finding.

The nine dirty files are committed and pushed. Five substantive fixes had sat uncommitted for at least eight days when this was raised; they went out earlier on 2026-09-22 in three commits, the for-sale licence gate, the shelved campaign proposal with its eight rulings, and the status writer keeping the paused and retired blocks. Verified now: git status is clean against HEAD 722516f and the branch is level with origin. The finding asked for the release script or a pathspec commit; a pathspec commit is what landed, which is the right half on a project stalled on budget since 2026-09-20, because a release is new work and a commit is finishing old work.

The write is still gated on an origin header, and that is a decision rather than an omission, recorded in the worker beside the gate. The finding asked for a server-validated editor credential. The only client that writes is the design document, served from key-value storage verbatim after a session cookie validates, so a credential that page could send is one anyone who opens it can read: an embedded token authenticates the document, not the editor. Doing it properly means the gate injecting a per-session token as it serves the page, which is an auth design on a project stalled since 2026-09-20 and exactly the spend D81 stops. What the endpoint holds is asset tracking, so the loss that matters is somebody replacing it with nothing. Every write keeps the copy it replaced now, three slots on a rotating index, and a failure to keep it does not fail the write. Shipped in 722516f; the 77-check preship passes.
